items.stem: Which addressing mode is described as: the operand is the value to be used?
options: Relative
Indexed
Direct
Immediate
items.answer: Immediate
items.markingKey: immediate: the operand is the value to be used; e.g. LDM #25.

items.stem: Explain why indirect addressing is useful.
items.answer: The address held in memory can be changed at run time, so the same instruction can access different locations (like a pointer); it also allows access to a larger address range.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between direct and indexed addressing.
items.answer: Direct uses the operand as the address; indexed adds the index register to the operand to form the address, so the same instruction can access a sequence of locations.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: An embedded system at MetroBus in Kuala Lumpur processes a table of sensor readings in assembly language. (a) Describe the difference between immediate and indirect addressing. (b) Explain one reason why relative addressing is used for jumps.
items.answer: (a) Immediate: operand is the value. Indirect: operand is an address whose contents is the address of the value. (b) Code is relocatable; branch targets stay correct wherever the program is loaded.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: What is the main feature of imperative programming?
options: The program has no variables
The program is a set of objects only
The program is a sequence of statements that change the program state (values of variables)
The program states facts and rules
items.answer: The program is a sequence of statements that change the program state (values of variables)
items.markingKey: It describes how to solve a problem step by step.

items.stem: Procedural programming is imperative programming that
options: uses only facts and rules
cannot use loops
only uses machine code
is structured into procedures and functions
items.answer: is structured into procedures and functions
items.markingKey: e.g. Python, Pascal, C, Cambridge pseudocode.

items.stem: Explain the difference between imperative and declarative programming.
items.answer: Imperative: the programmer gives the steps (how) that change state; declarative: the programmer states facts/rules (what) and the system works out how to find the answer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem:
Study the procedural program:
DECLARE Count : INTEGER
Count ← 2
PROCEDURE Update()
    Count ← Count * 2
    OUTPUT Count
ENDPROCEDURE
CALL Update()
CALL Update()
OUTPUT Count
What is output?
items.markingKey: No local declaration, so the procedure changes the global Count each call.

items.stem:
Sipho has written a procedural program for Summit Engineering and a colleague suggests an object-oriented version. (a) Part of the program is shown:
DECLARE Count : INTEGER
Count ← 7
PROCEDURE Update()
    DECLARE Count : INTEGER
    Count ← 28
    OUTPUT Count
ENDPROCEDURE
CALL Update()
OUTPUT Count
State the output. Explain your answer with reference to the scope of the variables. (b) Explain why parameters are preferred to global variables.
items.answer: (a) 28 7 (b) Makes subroutines independent and reusable; reduces side effects; easier testing.
items.markingKey: (a) output 28 7 [1]; the procedure declares a local Count that hides the global one; the global Count is unchanged [1] [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Procedural programming is imperative programming that (b) What is the main feature of imperative programming?
items.answer: (a) is structured into procedures and functions (b) The program is a sequence of statements that change the program state (values of variables)
items.markingKey: (a) e.g. Python, Pascal, C, Cambridge pseudocode. (b) It describes how to solve a problem step by step.

items.stem: Explain why using local variables rather than global variables is good practice in procedural programming.
items.answer: Subroutines are self-contained, so they can be tested and reused independently; there is less risk of accidentally changing a value used elsewhere.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

A is true but R is false

items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A and R are both true statements, but R does not explain A.

items.stem: Harbour Bank in Doha is choosing a paradigm for a new payroll program. (a) Describe the features of procedural programming. (b) Compare procedural and object-oriented programming for a large project.
items.answer: (a) Sequence of instructions; procedures/functions with parameters; local and global variables; selection and iteration; state changed by assignment. (b) OOP: encapsulation, reuse through inheritance, easier maintenance by teams; procedural: simpler, efficient for smaller tasks, data and functions separate.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 3 [3] (b) 1 mark per point, max 3 [3]

items.stem: In declarative programming, the programmer writes
options: machine code
facts and rules, and the system finds answers to goals (queries)
a step-by-step algorithm
classes and objects only
items.answer: facts and rules, and the system finds answers to goals (queries)
items.markingKey: The programmer states what, not how.

items.stem: Explain what is meant by backtracking in declarative programming.
items.answer: When a goal fails (or more solutions are wanted) the system goes back to the most recent choice point and tries the next matching fact or rule.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain why declarative languages are suited to expert systems.
items.answer: Knowledge is naturally expressed as facts and rules; the inference engine searches them to answer queries, so new knowledge can be added easily without rewriting algorithms.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) What does the symbol :- mean in a Prolog rule? (b) How does Prolog find answers to a goal?

items.stem: Isla is writing a Prolog knowledge base about family relationships for a genealogy app developed in Bangkok. (a) Explain the difference between a fact and a rule. (b) Describe how the system answers a goal.
items.answer: (a) A fact is unconditionally true (e.g. parent(a, b).); a rule is true if its conditions are satisfied (head :- body). (b) Searches facts and rules in order; unifies variables with matching values; uses backtracking to find alternative solutions.

items.stem: Tariq is writing assembly code for a microcontroller used by City Central Library. (a) Describe the difference between immediate and indirect addressing. (b) Explain one reason why relative addressing is used for jumps.
items.answer: (a) Immediate: operand is the value. Indirect: operand is an address whose contents is the address of the value. (b) Code is relocatable; branch targets stay correct wherever the program is loaded.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: An embedded system at Nova Telecom in Madrid processes a table of sensor readings in assembly language. (a) Explain why indexed addressing is suitable for processing the table of readings. (b) Describe the difference between immediate and indirect addressing. (c) Explain one reason why relative addressing is used for jumps.
items.answer: (a) IX is incremented each pass of a loop, so the same LDX instruction reads successive elements. (b) Immediate: operand is the value. Indirect: operand is an address whose contents is the address of the value. (c) Code is relocatable; branch targets stay correct wherever the program is loaded.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark each [2] (c) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: What is a global variable?

Total ← 12
